subject.title: [Bug] Cron Job 使用错误的飞书账号发送消息 - 缺少 accountId 自动推断

question: For cron announce delivery with `agentId` and no `delivery.accountId`, should OpenClaw prefer a same-channel session `lastAccountId`, the agent/channel binding, or fail closed when those can disagree?
rationale: This changes account identity selection for scheduled sends, so automation cannot safely choose between compatibility with current session-first behavior and the security goal of preventing cross-account delivery.

options.title: Fail closed on ambiguity
options.body: Keep explicit `delivery.accountId` highest, use a binding only when no conflicting session account is present or the route proves the same account, and otherwise refuse with a clear cron diagnostic.

options.title: Prefer agent binding
options.body: Make the bound agent/channel account outrank session history for cron delivery, accepting that existing jobs relying on session account drift may change behavior.

options.title: Keep session-first
options.body: Preserve current compatibility and document that multi-account cron jobs must set `delivery.accountId` explicitly to avoid wrong-account sends.

recommendation.title: Fail closed on ambiguity
recommendation.body: Keep explicit `delivery.accountId` highest, use a binding only when no conflicting session account is present or the route proves the same account, and otherwise refuse with a clear cron diagnostic.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the original binding-fallback work and is the clearest available owner signal for a security/product routing decision.
